I'm a reporter interested in covering Senate races. 

I think your question is better asked of the billionaire out of staters spending millions of dollars funding a Republican super PAC that's trying to buy your state's election.


kellie - bring back sanity please. (@kellie6666)

This will be my second time asking , why are you  out of staters  ( like you ) so interested in this Maine senate race. Is it about the Maine people or your unwavering thirst for power and control via the D ticket.

Find the piece here - and pass it on 

sirota.substack.com/p/bernie…

This is my theory. 

It may be wrong & I don't know if it will play out exactly like the Goldwater-to-Reagan juggernaut that changed the course of history. 

But there are already similarities - and we are only in year 10 of the 16-20 year cycle.

It's about to get interesting.
A different way to say this is: Bernie is the Goldwater — he lost the presidential race but won the larger ideological battle inside the party. The corporatists have lost — at least for now.

Reagan ran in the GOP's Goldwater Lane after Goldwater's loss - Reagan lost once in that lane ('76) & then won. Had he heeded your claim about lanes not being winning if someone lost in them, there wouldnt have been a Reagan Revolution. Your tweet ignores how history often works.


Stephen Robinson (Bluesky at @playtyperguy.com) (@SER1897)

Sanders ran twice and lost — arguably performing worse the second time. If you run, you should run in a winning lane.



— https://nitter.net/SER1897/sta
